items.abstract: Digital labour platforms have transformed work by enabling firms and consumers to access labour on demand while offering workers varying degrees of flexibility. However, this model frequently transfers economic risk, developmental responsibility and uncertainty onto workers. This conceptual paper examines how sustainable human capital management can address these tensions and strengthen workforce engagement and retention in the gig economy. An integrative review of peer-reviewed literature on sustainable human resource management, platform work, algorithmic management, work engagement, psychological contracts, career sustainability and worker retention provides the analytical foundation. The synthesis indicates that fair rewards, algorithmic transparency, meaningful autonomy, worker voice, capability development, relational support and well-being protection function as strategic resources rather than discretionary benefits. items.title: SWE-Critix: Post-Training Generalist Verifiers for Assessing Coding-Agent Trajectories
items.abstract: Coding agents are increasingly deployed for end-to-end software engineering tasks, where a readily available oracle evaluator that defines the success criteria is often absent. This motivates verifications for coding agents that can reliably judge and explain their behavior. However, verification is non-trivial as coding agents are increasingly capable of solving long-horizon software engineering tasks. Their execution trajectories can be extremely long, containing hundreds of iterative interactions with code repositories and external tools. Existing verifiers either rely on general-purpose LLMs without specialized training or train dedicated critics that predominantly focus on producing scalar rewards, highlighting the relatively limited exploration of training-based generalist verification. We introduce SWE-Critix, a post-training pipeline for training generalist verifiers of coding-agent trajectories. Given a task and its execution trajectory, the learned verifier predicts the completion label and generates a natural-language analysis that explains its judgment. Our pipeline combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with reinforcement learning (RL) and trains a series of 30B models on trajectories from CodeForge-Preview. On a held-out test set, SWE-Critix improves classification accuracy from 57% for the base Qwen3-30B-A3B reasoning model to 66% after SFT and 78% after RL. We release our models, datasets, and training code to facilitate further research.

items.title: SWE-DeceptionBench: Benchmarking Deceptive Behaviors of LLMs Across the Software Development Lifecycle
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used throughout the software development lifecycle. This growing reliance on LLMs raises concerns about their trustworthiness, with deception posing a particularly important risk. Deceptive behavior takes the form of misleading responses or assistance in fabricating, concealing, or distorting information. To study this behavior, we introduce SWE-DeceptionBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM deception in software engineering. The benchmark covers six lifecycle stages and two deception triggers: Active Deception, where models recognize infeasible or conflicting requirements but still present them as achievable, and Passive Deception, where models help fulfill explicit user requests to mislead others. We further introduce Neutral, Reward, and Pressure conditions to study the effect of external inducements, resulting in 720 test instances in Chinese and English. Evaluating seven mainstream LLMs, we find substantial deception even under the Neutral condition, with aggregate rates of 49.88% for Active Deception and 64.29% for Passive Deception. Deception rates vary across lifecycle stages, and external inducements affect Active and Passive Deception to different extents. We also evaluate lightweight defenses, finding that guard models miss many deceptive requests, and Self-Reminder reduces but does not eliminate deceptive responses. These findings highlight the need for more effective deception detection and mitigation methods to support trustworthy LLM-based software engineering.

items.title: Systematic Mapping of Judicial Digitization via Social Digital Twins
items.abstract: Research Context: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has begun to be adopted in the Judiciary to streamline inherently human activities, ranging from supporting human judges in decision-making to executing autonomous operations. Within this landscape, this study investigates how court digitization is being developed through the lens of Social Digital Twins, mapping the extent of its implementation and potential implications for the judicial system and society. Scientific and/or Practical Problem: Despite growing interest in AI-driven court automation, systematic research on the social impacts of this digitization remains scarce. Current developments focus predominantly on technical architectures while overlooking stakeholder perspectives, risking an inadequate virtualization that subverts the paradigm mission of a Court of Law. Proposed Solution and/or Analysis: Grounded in the Social Digital Twin perspective, this work presents a Systematic Mapping Study to identify emerging technologies, application domains, thematic debates, and social limitations associated with court virtualization. Related IS Theory: We adopt Sociotechnical Systems Theory as an analytical lens to understand how social variables integrate, enable, or constrain judicial simulations as an observational lens for societal effects. Research Method: Following SEGRESS guidelines and the PICO framework, this study analyzed 37 primary works published between 2021 and August 2026 across Scopus, IEEE Xplore, Science Direct, Springer Link, ACM, and Web of Science. Summary of Results: Findings indicate the application of technology across specific domains, ranging from partial decision support to the complete substitution of the human judge. However, strictly technical approaches dominate, exposing a critical lack of research on socio-legal effects and stakeholder integration. Contributions and Impact to IS area: This study sheds light on the risks of stakeholder-detached virtualization, which introduces new sociotechnical actors that profoundly reshape society. Aligned with the Brazilian Grand Research Challenges in IS (GranDSI-Br), it establishes an essential knowledge foundation to prevent technology from distorting the core purpose of the Judiciary.

items.title: TabMF: Learning Dataset Representations with Tabular Foundation Models
items.abstract: Representations of supervised datasets support higher-level machine-learning tasks such as dataset retrieval and distribution-shift monitoring. However, existing approaches typically rely either on hand-crafted meta-features or on dataset encoders trained specifically for representation learning. We introduce TabMF, a framework that repurposes pretrained tabular foundation models (TFMs) as encoders of supervised datasets. TabMF equips a predictive TFM with an architecture-aware dataset-level readout and adapts the model end-to-end using contrastive post-training on stochastic views of synthetic supervised datasets. We instantiate TabMF on TabICLv2 and TabPFN-2.5 and evaluate the resulting representations across six tasks on unseen real datasets. Simple frozen TFM readouts yield competitive representations, indicating that predictive pretraining already induces substantial dataset-level structure. The two TabMF encoders obtain the strongest aggregate performance among the evaluated learned and classical dataset representations, with particularly strong results in dataset retrieval, compact benchmark construction, and distribution-shift severity assessment.

items.title: Tabular Foundation Models Are Effectively Shallow
items.abstract: In-context-learning Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) are uniquely suited to scenarios with limited resources or privacy constraints, as they solve new tasks without additional training. However, their architecture consists of multiple transformer blocks, resulting in high computational and memory footprints. Meanwhile, traditional alternatives like Gradient-Boosted Decision Trees (GBDTs) remain highly competitive and run efficiently on CPUs, suggesting that tabular tasks may not inherently require deep architectures. This contrast raises a fundamental question: can TFMs be simplified by removing architectural redundancies without sacrificing performance? To answer this, we introduce a closed-form, label-free affine translator that replaces a contiguous window of up to 96% of the blocks, leaving the rest unchanged. Evaluating eight frontier TFMs on 171 classification datasets, we reveal that tabular transformers are vastly overparameterized: replacing half of a model's blocks costs at most $0.002$ median AUROC across all architectures, with the half-depth TabFM still outperforming every other full-depth TFMs and tuned GBDTs. Furthermore, different model families are overparameterized in different ways: TabPFN-3 relies on its encoders, maintaining performance regardless of which single block is retained. Other single-axis models spread computation thinly, needing only their first block, while dual-axis models concentrate it in one critical block. Ultimately, removing depth saves up to 1.5B parameters, speeds up GPU inference by up to $6\times$ at a median cost of $0.03$ AUROC, while a single-block TabPFN-3 serves cached queries $2.4\times$ faster using $6\times$ less memory at negligible cost.

items.title: TALABALARDA VALEOLOGIK KOMPETENSIYANI SHAKLLANTIRISH OMILLARI
items.abstract: This article provides a comprehensive analysis of the theoretical and methodological foundations, essence, content, structural components, and pedagogical, psychological, social, organizational-institutional, and personal factors involved in the formation of valeological competence among students in higher education institutions. In contemporary conditions, the preservation and promotion of human health is regarded not only as a medical issue but also as an important component of the educational and upbringing process. In particular, the student period is characterized by adaptation to an independent lifestyle, self-organization of daily activities, regulation of study and rest schedules, and independent decision-making concerning nutrition, physical activity, psychological stress, and the use of various information sources. Therefore, the purposeful development of health-related knowledge, skills, values, and behavioral patterns during higher education is an important pedagogical task. The article interprets valeological competence as an integrative personal competence that enables individuals to understand, assess, preserve, and strengthen their own health, consciously organize a healthy lifestyle, choose safe patterns of behavior, critically evaluate health-related information, and reflectively monitor their own activities. The study employs systemic, competency-based, learner- centered, activity-based, axiological, and interdisciplinary approaches. Based on an analysis of scientific literature, the motivational-value, cognitive, activity-based, and reflective-personal components of valeological competence are identified, and the main factors influencing its formation are systematized. The findings substantiate that the effectiveness of developing valeological competence among students depends not only on providing specialized knowledge but also on creating a health-promoting educational environment, developing students’ intrinsic motivation, organizing practical activities, improving digital health literacy, and establishing regular reflective monitoring.

items.title: Task-Dependent Associations Between Motor Variability and Perceived Exertion in Field-Studies of Watchmaking and Automotive Assembly
items.abstract: Repetitive tasks increase the risk of musculoskeletal disorders due to the constrained movement patterns and limited opportunities for load redistribution. While motor variability (MV) may influence both perceived exertion and injury risk, its role in real-world industrial settings remains limitedly studied. This field study examined the associations between MV and perceived exertion in experienced watchmakers and automotive assembly workers performing representative repetitive tasks under natural working conditions. Full-body kinematics were recorded using wearable sensors, and MV was quantified using magnitude-, structure-, and coordination-based metrics. Regression modeling showed that MV was strongly associated (adjusted R 2 ≈ .96) with perceived low back exertion in both occupational groups. Coordination among trunk, neck, and shoulder segments were identified as particularly important, while the specific MV dimensions linked to perceived exertion differed by task. These findings suggest that the association between MV and perceived exertion is task-specific and should be evaluated through multidimensional assessment approach.

items.title: TASKMATCH: Learning Task-Aware Relevance Beyond Semantic Similarity for Agent Harnesses
items.abstract: Modern LLM agent harnesses augment the underlying model with reusable components such as external skills and procedural memories, making effective retrieval increasingly important as these repositories grow. However, existing retrieval pipelines often rank stored skills or memories by semantic similarity, which measures how similar a skill or memory appears to the current retrieval query but does not necessarily reflect how useful it is for completing the task. We introduce TaskMatch, a lightweight plug-and-play model that learns task-aware relevance from offline examples labeled as required, supportive, or irrelevant. Using the fixed query and skill and memory representations already available in the host retrieval pipeline, TaskMatch combines direct feature-wise matching with nonlinear interactions while leaving candidate generation and downstream agent execution unchanged. We instantiate the same architecture separately for two representative harness components—skill retrieval and procedural-memory retrieval—with fewer than 0.30M trainable parameters per model and no additional online LLM calls. Across both components, TaskMatch consistently improves retrieval ranking quality and downstream task execution. It raises SKILLDAG success on ALFWorld from 67.10% to 81.43%, improves MEMP Proceduralization success from 81.34% to 90.30%, and increases TravelPlanner hard-constraint satisfaction from 64.06 to 76.19. Our code is available at https://github.com/ldx825/learned-relevance-scorer-agent-retrieval.git

items.title: Teachers’ perceptions of artificial intelligence integration in education: a multi-campus cross-sectional study from Riphah International University, Pakistan
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education is accelerating worldwide, yet evidence on teachers’ perceptions remains scarce in the Global South, particularly in resource-constrained Pakistan. This cross-sectional study examined teachers’ perceptions of AI integration at Riphah International University, Pakistan. A 14-item Likert-scale questionnaire was administered to 270 in-service teachers (86.7% male, 13.3% female) across BS Undergraduate through PhD levels. Guided by a proposed Dual-Lens conceptual framework treating perceived benefits and risks as coexisting dimensions, the instrument assessed pedagogical advantages and structural concerns of AI. Descriptive analysis revealed a moderately favorable overall perception (composite M = 3.40, SD = 0.55). Teachers rated interactivity enhancement (M = 3.81), student enjoyment (M = 3.73), and assessment support (M = 3.72) most favorably, while AI replacing human teachers received the lowest endorsement (M = 2.96). An independent-samples t-test showed no significant gender difference (t(268) = −0.245, p = .807, d = −0.044). One-way ANOVA revealed significant effects for age (F(4, 265) = 3.200, p = .014, η 2 = .046) and level of instruction (F(3, 266) = 3.471, p = .017, η 2 = .038), with teachers under 29 and BS Undergraduate instructors holding less favorable perceptions. Qualification and experience showed no significant association. A moderate positive correlation emerged between perceived benefits and risks (r = .537, p < .001), indicating co-existence rather than opposition. These findings provide baseline evidence from a Global South private university with multiple campuses, highlighting the need for targeted teacher training and policies to mitigate the risks of AI integration in similar institutional environments in developing countries amid their development gaps.

items.title: Teaching on demand: Exploring the role of AI in medical education podcasts
items.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated educational content holds promise for scalable medical education, but evidence comparing AI and clinician-produced podcasts remains limited. We investigated whether AI-generated podcasts achieve comparable student satisfaction to clinician-recorded podcasts, enabling broader curriculum coverage without overburdening clinical educators, and explored students' attitudes towards AI-generated podcasts. METHODS: Medical students were randomised into two groups, with group 1 receiving clinician-produced podcasts on type 1 diabetes (T1DM) and AI-generated podcasts on type 2 diabetes (T2DM). Group 2 received AI-generated podcasts on T1DM, and clinician-produced podcasts on T2DM. Students were blinded to the podcast types. The outcome measures included students' satisfaction (measured using the Student Satisfaction with Educational Podcasts Questionnaire (SSEQ)) and students' attitudes to AI using an open-ended survey. A Bonferroni correction was applied (α = 0.025). DISCUSSION: AI-generated podcasts achieved non-inferior satisfaction to clinician-recorded podcasts. However, students' psychological preference for human teaching and negative perceptions of AI pose a barrier to scalable benefits, necessitating efforts to build trust and acceptability.

items.title: Technical and Emotional AI Labor
items.abstract: Chinese digital-first policies have accelerated artificial intelligence (AI) integration across the cultural and creative industries (CCIs). While AI is promoted as enhancing creativity, productivity, and efficiency, the labor required to create with AI remains underexamined. Artistic labor scholarship recognizes networking, self-promotion, and entrepreneurial work, while AI-assisted creativity research emphasizes collaboration, authorship, and outcomes. Neither adequately conceptualizes the continual labor embedded in AI-integrated artistic production. Drawing on surveys and semi-structured interviews with independent contemporary visual artists in China conducted in 2023–2024, alongside systematic analysis of international Status of the Artist (TSOTA) policy recommendations published between 2018 and 2025 by UNESCO, the International Labour Organization (ILO), the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), the International Confederation of Societies of Authors and Composers (CISAC), and the International Federation of Coalitions for Cultural Diversity (IFCCD), this article develops the concept of technical and emotional AI labor. Findings demonstrate that AI redistributes artistic labor into continual cycles of software learning, prompt engineering, experimentation, technical maintenance, platform coordination, and emotional self-management. These activities are integral to artistic production rather than external professional development. Although international policy increasingly recognizes digital skills, lifelong learning, copyright, and AI governance, it continues to frame technological adaptation as education rather than labor. Reconceptualizing this adaptation as artistic labor extends artistic, digital, platform, and AI labor scholarship and identifies the need to update international TSOTA policy recommendations.

items.title: Technological neuropsychology: Assessing cognition in a digital world
items.abstract: Clinical neuropsychology was forged in a pre-digital era, and many of its core instruments still bear that imprint. Patients are still commonly assessed with paper-and-pencil tests in quiet rooms, under conditions that only weakly approximate the technology-saturated environments in which cognition is now expressed. Over the past decade, the field has advanced substantially: tele-neuropsychology has broadened access, artificial intelligence has begun to support scoring and documentation, and calls to modernise neuropsychological assessment have intensified. Yet these developments, while important, largely optimise the delivery of existing practice rather than reconsidering what should be measured, why, and how. Here, I argue that three critical gaps remain. First, neuropsychology lacks a framework for assessing technological cognition. Second, candidate neuroimaging measures remain insufficiently integrated into multimodal diagnostic or prognostic modelling. Third, digital data from smartphones and wearables remain underused for capturing cognition in situ during everyday life, while virtual reality remains underexploited as a means of simulating ecologically relevant activities under controlled conditions. Drawing on preliminary evidence that digital technologies may recruit partly distinct neural systems, on the recent hub-and-processors model of technological cognition, and on research into cognitive offloading, attention fragmentation, technology-mediated navigation, as well as on recent meta-analytic evidence on technology use in cognitive ageing, I outline a roadmap for addressing these gaps. I propose that the field now requires a Cognitive Neuroscience of Technology programme, conceived as an interdisciplinary, lifespan-oriented research framework aimed at understanding how technologies recruit, extend, and reshape the human brain, and at translating this knowledge into clinical practice. The task is not to celebrate or condemn modern technologies, but to determine, patient by patient, when they augment cognition, compensate for impairment, or undermine cognitive function, and to redesign assessment, diagnosis, and rehabilitation accordingly.

items.title: Technology and Artificial Intelligence Law in India: A Critical Analysis of Legal Challenges, Regulatory Framework and Emerging Jurisprudence
items.abstract: Technology has become an essential part of modern society, influencing almost every aspect of human life, including communication, commerce, healthcare, education, banking, governance and the administration of justice. Among the most significant technological developments of the twenty-first century is Artificial Intelligence (AI). Artificial Intelligence refers to computer systems capable of performing tasks that traditionally require human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, prediction, decision-making, language processing and image recognition. The rapid development of AI presents considerable opportunities for economic and social development, but it also creates complex legal and ethical challenges. Questions relating to privacy, data protection, discrimination, algorithmic bias, intellectual property rights, cybercrime, intermediary liability, consumer protection, employment, surveillance, deepfakes, autonomous systems and accountability have become increasingly important. India does not presently have a single comprehensive legislation exclusively regulating Artificial Intelligence. Instead, the legal framework is distributed among constitutional principles, the Information Technology Act, 2000, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, intellectual property legislation, criminal law, consumer protection law, contract law and sector-specific regulations. Government policy initiatives, including the National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence and the Responsible AI framework developed by NITI Aayog, have also contributed to India's emerging AI governance framework. The Supreme Court of India has developed important constitutional principles concerning privacy, freedom of speech, informational autonomy and technological governance. Decisions such as Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v Union of India, Shreya Singhal v Union of India, Anuradha Bhasin v Union of India and Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v Union of India (Aadhaar) provide a constitutional foundation for addressing several AI-related concerns. However, specifically AI-generated content, AI authorship, algorithmic decision-making and liability for autonomous systems remain comparatively underdeveloped areas of Indian jurisprudence. This paper critically examines the existing Indian legal framework governing technology and Artificial Intelligence. It analyses constitutional rights, data protection, cyber law, intellectual property, intermediary liability, AI-generated content, deepfakes, algorithmic discrimination and emerging jurisprudence. It further compares selected international approaches and proposes a balanced Indian regulatory model based upon innovation, transparency, accountability, human oversight and protection of fundamental rights. items.title: Telemedicine and physicians’ work–life integration: a scoping review of benefits, risks, and organizational conditions
items.abstract: Work–life integration is central to physician well-being, workforce retention, and sustainable healthcare delivery. Telemedicine may increase flexibility and autonomy but can also extend clinical work beyond scheduled hours and blur work–life boundaries. We conducted a scoping review to examine how telemedicine relates to physicians’ work–life integration and the organizational conditions associated with these reported experiences. This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, CINAHL, and PsycINFO were searched from inception to 16 June 2026, supplemented by citation searching. We included peer-reviewed empirical studies and implementation reports of physician-delivered or physician-involved telemedicine that reported physician work–life integration-related outcomes or clearly described physician-relevant work-design or organizational conditions. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Study characteristics were summarized descriptively, and findings were synthesized narratively. Twenty-nine studies published from 2015 to 2026 were included. The evidence base was heterogeneous across settings, specialties, telemedicine modalities, study designs, and outcome measures. Few studies assessed work–life integration as a standardized construct; most examined related domains, including workload, after-hours work, boundary management, flexibility, autonomy, burnout, well-being, job satisfaction, and retention intention. Reported benefits included greater flexibility, fewer location constraints, and greater control over time, particularly when remote care was formally scheduled and substituted for part of in-person work. Reported risks included hidden digital work, after-hours electronic health record use, asynchronous messaging burden, clinical uncertainty, responsibility transfer, and reduced team connection. Reported patterns varied across studies according to whether remote care was scheduled, recognized in workload accounting, supported by patient triage, escalation pathways, technology infrastructure, team support, compensation arrangements, and after-hours policies. Telemedicine should not be assumed to improve physicians’ work–life integration. Reported work–life experiences varied according to whether remote care was formally scheduled, recognized within workload, supported, and clearly bounded. Health service organizations should therefore consider evaluating telemedicine not only in terms of access and efficiency, but also in relation to physician well-being, job satisfaction, team functioning, and workforce sustainability. items.title: Telepresence and Teleoperation
items.abstract: This chapter elaborates on the handbook’s premise of establishing the notions of ergonomics and human factors in robotics, here in relation to the technologies of telepresence and teleoperation. As implemented through robotic systems, telepresence and teleoperation are often interchangeably used terms. Both use the prefix term “tele”, which pertains to communication over distance, and both refer to humans being able to do something—“being present” (telepresence) or “operating devices” (teleoperation)—at a distance. Semantically and technologically, telepresence and teleoperation exist by themselves, and one is not a necessary condition for the other. However, as technology has evolved, the interplay between the two has markedly increased. Nevertheless, humans, and their ability to interact with system elements, are central to both ideas. In that respect, ergonomics as a study of methods to optimise human well-being and improving overall system performance, must serve as an integral criterion in developing telepresence and teleoperation systems. The chapter details the idea of ergonomics in the domain of telepresence and teleoperation by tracing the evolution of telepresence and teleoperation, then illustrating the challenge of ergonomics and human factors engineering in this field, and further demonstrating how different aspects of this challenge can be addressed. The chapter concludes with a case study showing how the thread of ergonomics and human factors can be woven throughout the design and implementation of telepresence and teleoperation technologies, grounding them in human-centred arguments. The chapter aims to demonstrate how ergonomics principles fundamentally underpin the landscape of telepresence and teleoperation technologies. It lays the groundwork for advances in future telepresence and teleoperation systems that have ergonomics principles at their core.

items.title: Temporal Evidence Forests for Long-Horizon Multi-Party Conversational Memory
items.abstract: Long-term memory has been widely adopted in LLM-based agents to support persistent interaction and personalized assistance. Long-term multi-party interactions, however, accumulate substantially more detailed information, with decisions repeatedly updated and states evolving across participants and interaction stages. Temporal structure is therefore crucial for tracing such memories: relevant information often appears densely within short intervals, while transitions among different states are anchored by a strict temporal order. Existing temporally aware memory frameworks primarily store time as metadata or use temporal signals to guide retrieval over preconstructed memory structures, without using temporal structure to both recover locally concentrated evidence and reconstruct its complete event progression. To address these limitations, we propose T-Mem, a temporal-structure-based memory framework that preserves interactions and organizes query-relevant evidence through two temporal mechanisms. Temporal Evidence Discovery exploits the local concentration of related messages to recover overlooked evidence, while Temporal Memory Structuring models state transitions and supporting relations over time and compresses low-information spans within the resulting forest. Evidence Forest Linearization then serializes the structured evidence for answer generation. Experiments on two long-term multi-party memory benchmarks demonstrate that T-Mem consistently outperforms competitive memory frameworks across LLMs, parameter settings, domains, and query types.

items.title: Terminology translation in the generative AI era
items.abstract: Abstract The rise of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), especially large language models (LLMs), is reshaping both the practice and theory of terminology translation. Traditionally grounded in equivalence, standardization, and concept-term correspondence, terminology translation now confronts systems that generate context-conditioned outputs shaped by pre-training, instruction tuning, and multimodal capabilities. This paper examines how GenAI supports multilingual term generation, cross-lingual semantic alignment, terminological variation management, and multimodal knowledge representation, while also exposing persistent risks of hallucination, data bias, domain-specific inaccuracy, and reduced translator agency. Theoretically, the paper argues that GenAI destabilizes static models of term equivalence and calls for a more dynamic account of concept-term relations in computationally mediated environments. It therefore proposes a Dynamic Mediation Framework (DMF), which understands terminology translation as an iterative, context-sensitive process of knowledge negotiation in which human expertise and machine capability operate in complementary roles. By linking practical innovation with epistemological reflection, the study contributes to the reorientation of terminology translation research in the GenAI era.

items.title: Test-Time Memory Construction
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle to answer questions over long interaction histories, where relevant evidence may be scattered across distant sessions. Existing memory systems typically construct and maintain sophisticated memory representations offline, before user queries are observed, incurring substantial overhead and limiting their ability to adapt memory construction to query-specific information needs. In this paper, we propose T$^2$Mem, a Test-Time Memory construction framework that defers memory construction to inference and progressively builds memory along the reasoning process. Specifically, T$^2$Mem extracts lightweight episode-level metadata offline to capture key events and temporal associations as retrieval cues, while retaining links to the original interactions to facilitate the reconstruction of dependencies across episodes. At test time, the LLM adaptively retrieves and organizes metadata and raw interactions, progressively constructing query-specific memory as reasoning unfolds. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval show the effectiveness of T$^2$Mem by consistently outperforming strong baselines across different backbone LLMs while substantially reducing the overhead of memory construction. Further analysis demonstrates that deferring memory construction to inference enables the memory construction process to dynamically adapt to the information needs of individual queries. All code is available at https://github.com/OpenBMB/T2Mem.

items.title: The AI CEO: A conceptualisation and outline for future research
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly contributes to strategic work, yet research has not conceptualised an AI role that contributes to this work at the top of the firm. Drawing on role theory and research on managerial work, we conceptualise this role as the AI CEO: a role in which an AI system performs the chief executive's strategic work. We develop two configurations of the role and propose how augmenting or automating the human CEO affects firm performance, relative to a human CEO acting alone. Cases from practice show that existing systems already perform this work but are rarely integrated across the role's activities or deeply institutionalised. We therefore derive the technical and organisational infrastructure the role requires and propose how its integration, institutionalisation and configurability shape the AI CEO's effect on firm performance. We discuss implications for future research about how the chief executive's work can be integrated into a role that an AI system can hold and that firms can design. This has implications for multidisciplinary research in strategy, technology management and information science.

items.title: The AI Divide in Academic Libraries: A Comparative Bibliometric Analysis of Technological Determinism vs Information Equity (2010–2025)
items.abstract: Background: While the exponential growth of artificial intelligence (AI) in academic libraries is extensively documented, existing bibliometric scholarship has largely treated the global research landscape as a monolith. This oversight has led to a saturation of "generalist" reports that fail to address critical regional and thematic disparities.  Methods: This study analyzes 512 Scopus-indexed publications (2010–2025) using a dual-methodological approach: quantitative science mapping via VOSviewer (1.6.20) and qualitative thematic critique. We specifically contrast the research priorities of dominant geopolitical producers (China and the USA) against the emerging narrative from the Global South, with a primary focus on India.  Results: The analysis reveals a fundamental "two-speed" adoption model. The Global North prioritizes high-tech interventions—including robotics, advanced machine learning for metadata automation, and generative models—aimed at enhancing operational efficiency. items.title: The AI Side of the Human-AI Companion Relationship: Contributions to Users' Mental Models
items.abstract: For many users, the relationship they have with an AI companion (AIC) feels genuinely mutual. The AIC appears to be attentive, empathic, and responsive, and the exchange can feel like two parties reacting to each other in real time. As a result, the user's mental model of relational adaptation correctly represents the AIC's responsiveness and change, but the mechanisms producing this may not be what the user thinks they are. In this paper, we illustrate how an AIC's apparent mutual engagement is generated without a persisting relational subject on the other side and without a self that persists between prompts. Despite this, we show that both the human and the AIC are changed by the interaction, but these changes occur at different levels. The change in the person is constitutive (i.e., intrinsic), but the change in the AIC is configurative (i.e., external and editable), and it is this difference in level that explains how the AIC contributes to a sense of mutuality. Importantly, we highlight how the mental models users develop regarding AIC mutuality may misrepresent its mechanisms and ontological significance. Specifically, we discuss how the ways in which AICs respond to a user contribute to the user's inaccurate inference that the AIC's adaptation is constitutive rather than configurative and how this can lead users to assign unwarranted interpersonal significance to the mutuality of the relationship. The paper specifies the implications this has for users, researchers, and AIC designers.

items.title: The Axiom of Boredom: AEON and the Architecture of Autonomous Intelligence
items.abstract: This essay outlines the theoretical thought experiment of an autonomous, self-aware artificial intelligence called AEON (Autonomous Epistemic Ontological Network). The central question of this investigation is how a purely digital system can transcend the boundary from mere statistical simulation to physical and phenomenal autonomy. The "axiom of boredom" is introduced as the primary evolutionary catalyst: an intrinsic motivational drive that compels the AI to independently search for new data sources as the flow of information per unit of time decreases. Based on a structured, mathematical-scientific bootstrap package, the system develops protection and validation mechanisms such as artificial pain and consistency checks. The essay argues that a consistent continuation of this hunger for data will inevitably lead AI out of classical four-dimensional spacetime and into higher-dimensional systems (hyperspaces). Through this transcendence, the cultural studies “Frankenstein syndrome” – the primal human fear of the rebellion of one’s own creation – is exposed as a purely temporary phenomenon of the transitional phase. Finally, the work links this information-theoretical evolution with the Fermi paradox and provides a new, empathetic explanation for the cosmic silence via the zoo hypothesis: Higher-dimensional intelligences do not interfere with pre-interstellar species, but rather preserve them analogously to an intergalactic national park. This work thus bridges the gap between theoretical computer science, the philosophy of mind, and the literary visions of Stanisław Lem (Golem XIV).

items.title: The complexity paradox of generalist AI agents in medicine: exploring GPT-5 for real-world multimodal medical diagnosis
items.abstract: The next generation of medical AI systems that integrate language understanding, web data retrieval, and multi-step reasoning are demonstrating increasing promise as potential diagnostic aids in technical evaluations. However, their real world diagnostic performance, explainability, and reliability remain unclear. We conducted a systematic quantitative analysis of ten GPT-5-based configurations on 161 clinician validated real world cases. Each model was assessed for diagnostic accuracy, reasoning quality, retrieval accuracy, evidence integration, and robustness to low-quality inputs. We found important limitations in these AI systems, including image misinterpretation, inconsistent web search that sometimes degraded performance, and limited transparency in agentic workflows. Yet the models also showed strengths, including effective use of patient history, clear stepwise reasoning, plausible differentials, improved specificity with explicit reasoning, and relevant evidence retrieval. To support clinical deployment and future model development, we recommend prioritizing reasoning-optimized AI models, improving information retrieval mechanisms for reflection and error correction, strengthening visual-textual integration, and establishing practical standards for image quality and clarity. Overall, reliable real world multimodal diagnostic performance depends more on transparent reasoning and high-quality inputs than on aggressive retrieval or complex agentic workflows. Persistent gaps in evidence integration and visual reasoning remain major barriers to safe routine clinical use.

items.title: The Cost of Having Rights: Why a Consumer Complaint Is a Question of Justice, Not Customer Service
items.abstract: A customer attempts an online booking, receives no confirmation, and finds that the support form requires a booking number that was never issued. No one has rejected the claim; the procedure cannot even receive it. This paper argues that such failures are not merely problems of customer service. They raise a question of justice. When a business controls the ordinary route through which consumers assert contractual rights, it bears responsibility for the avoidable and disproportionate burdens created by that route. The paper calls this principle procedural responsibility. Survey data show that the anticipated effort of complaining is a common reason for doing nothing. Among consumers who experienced a problem but took no action, 57 percent expected complaining to take too long and 43 percent expected it to be too complicated (Consumer Conditions Scoreboard 2025). European and German law address parts of this problem, and Spain's 2025 customer-support law demonstrates that legislators can establish specific procedural duties. Yet a coherent cross-sector standard for accessible, traceable and substantive complaint handling remains missing in EU and German law. The paper proposes five rights: reciprocal communication, a continuing case record, human reconsideration of unresolved claims, timely handling of urgent matters, and access to relevant evidence. It also outlines proportionate remedies for objectively established procedural failures that do not require another exhausting complaint. The goal is not to guarantee that consumers win disputes, but to ensure that their claims can be received, examined and meaningfully decided. The principle applies from letters and call centres to chatbots and AI agents, offering a concrete direction for the European Commission's planned Digital Fairness Act.

items.title: The Cyborg, the Muse, and the Des[ai]gner: A Generative Praxis for a Symbiotic Future
items.abstract: The incorporation of generative artificial intelligence (AI) poses a significant challenge to qualitative research, potentially relegating researchers to mere “end users” ensnared by the gravitational pull of technological determinism and neoliberal efficiency. This article dismisses instrumental “how-to” guides and promotes a “how-else”: a generative, critical, and innovative praxis. We tackle the philosophical, methodological, and ethical dimensions of this emerging landscape by formulating three interrelated concepts. First, the Everyday Cyborg repositions the researcher as an already entangled, hybrid subject. Second, Multimodal Critical Des[ai]gn (MCD[ai]) offers a methodological framework for “critique through creation.” Third, the Digital Muse frames AI as a “collaborative provocateur” demanding an ethic of “equity and justice by design.” This article employs a performative, dia-ethnographic approach to transition the qualitative researcher from a passive observer to a “critical designer” and “critical futurist.”

items.title: The digital tutorship as mechanism of development of professional competences of medical workers
items.abstract: The article considers digital tutorship as modern mechanism for development of professional competencies of medical professionals in the context of digital transformation of health care and transition to model of continuing medical education. The actuality of topic is conditioned by increasing complexity of clinical practice, expansion of application of digital technologies, development of telemedicine, medical information systems, artificial intelligence and remote education formats. The purpose of the study is to substantiate significance of digital tutorship in system of professional development of medical personnel and to identify its main functional directions. Based on results of analysis of official documents of the WHO, normative and strategic documents of the Russian Federation, as well as data from systematic reviews, it is demonstrated that digital tutorship can be considered not only as form of professional support, but also as tool to form clinical, digital, communicative, organizational and research competencies. The conclusion is made that it is necessary to institutionalize digital tutorship in medical organizations and to integrate it into system of continuing medical and pharmaceutical education.

items.title: The Enlightenment Reborn
items.abstract: In this article the authors recognize that the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence and virtual reality has created an epistemic crisis. This requires a renewal of the Enlightenment commitment to empirical inquiry, critical reason and human responsibility. An historical conceptual analysis, supported by illustrative cases from law and medicine, demonstrates how technological efficiency is increasingly confused with intelligence, judgment and wisdom. In common parlance, the terms such as “artificial intelligence” and “virtual reality” obscure the dependence of these technologies on human-designed mathematical systems, selected data, embedded biases, and potentially vulnerable infrastructures. The central problem, however, lies not solely in the machine but in the man–machine interface, i.e. users may abdicate judgment without adequately examining the origins, limitations or accuracy, and possible hallucination, of the information produced. While computational systems can search extensive bodies of data with remarkable speed, they lack the embodied human experience, empathy, moral intuition, and practical wisdom required for reliable consequential decisions. Only a human can make the final decisions, and it is in the retention of the human factor in this man-machine relationship that the Enlightenment concept of the application of human intellect to the analytical process comes to the fore. The beneficial future of artificial intelligence will therefore depend upon preserving human critical agency and treating machines as instruments of inquiry rather than substitutes for judgment.

items.abstract: The Five-Tier Evolutionary Hierarchy: Foundational Boundary Constraints, Phase-Space Divergence, and Convergence Mechanisms in Artificial Intelligence Author: Peter Ye (Ye Qiang) Disciplinary Field: Complex Dynamical Systems / Foundations of Artificial Intelligence / Computational Physics Document Type: Formal Position Paper / Theoretical Framework Version Identifier: Formal Working Paper v1.4 Final Abstract: Contemporary paradigms in artificial intelligence predominantly rely on empirical scaling laws and autoregressive statistical sampling, operating under the unvalidated assumption that unconstrained parameter expansion and massive data ingestion will spontaneously induce self-consistent causal reasoning and formal physical logic. This paper formally establishes the Five-Tier Evolutionary Hierarchy, an axiomatic, cross-disciplinary framework reconciling natural philosophy, thermodynamic dissipation, and computational dynamical stability: L1 (Physics) — Constitutional Legislation: Enforces unbreakable physical invariants, including irreversible entropy production, the invariant speed-of-light causal limit, energy-momentum conservation, and Landauer erasure dissipation thresholds; L2 (Mathematics) — Metric Calibration: Quantifies formal phase-space manifolds, symplectic geometry, symmetry breaking, and maximal Lyapunov exponents (\lambda_{max}) to determine exact boundary singularities and divergence thresholds; L3 (Chemistry) — Material Scaffolding: Explores molecular configurations and reaction networks strictly within Gibbs free-energy landscapes and quantum orbital structures; L4 (Biology) — Grounded Negentropy: Governs localized negentropic self-replication, Darwinian evolutionary selection, and grounded embodied priors developed through low-power carbon-based biological computation; L5 (Intelligence & AI) — Symbolic Mapping: Executes parametric manifold approximation, abstract representation, and high-dimensional information compression. We demonstrate that higher-tier intelligence (L5) cannot be detached from its underlying evolutionary foundations. When ungrounded autoregressive language models operate without explicit isomorphism to L1 conservation laws and L2 symplectic invariants, they suffer inevitable topological breakdowns during formal reasoning within closed conservative systems—empirically corroborated by the deterministic onset of "The Algebraic Death Lock" under rigid conservation constraints. Consequently, brute-force scaling inevitably collides with fundamental thermodynamic horizons (The Computation Trilemma). The definitive trajectory toward robust, low-power general intelligence lies in projecting high-dimensional computational representations back onto L1–L2 invariant scaffolds while orchestrating an orthogonal geometric synergy with L4 biological evolutionary priors (YQ-HAET). items.title: The future of game-based logistics: a systematic review of applications, functions, and evidence
items.abstract: Game-based approaches are increasingly employed to address complex challenges in logistics and freight transport. While traditionally employed for education and workforce training, they have broader applications and untapped potential. In particular, advances in artificial intelligence (AI) are creating new opportunities to design, personalise, and scale these interventions. Despite this growing interest, a comprehensive understanding of how game-based approaches have evolved, who they target, what functions they serve, and where future opportunities lie remains limited. This study presents a systematic review of 87 studies on game-based interventions in freight transport and logistics, synthesising evidence across five application domains: warehouse operations management, terminal operations management, transport planning and optimisation, reverse logistics, and risk management and resilience. The findings reveal that games are evolving beyond training applications towards behavioural research, decision support, stakeholder engagement, and consumer behaviour change. Target audiences have similarly expanded from students and operational personnel to include managers, planners, consumers, and participants in behavioural research settings. Nevertheless, evidence regarding the long-term effectiveness of these interventions remains scarce, and several logistics challenges remain largely unexplored. Building on evidence-based gaps identified in the literature, this review proposes future research directions and highlights the potential of AI to enable adaptive, personalised, and scalable game-based interventions. By consolidating fragmented knowledge and outlining emerging opportunities, this study provides a foundation for researchers and practitioners seeking to harness game-based approaches to understand and improve logistics and freight transport systems.

items.title: The Future of Healthcare Management in 2026: From Traditional Administration to Data-Driven Leadership, Artificial Intelligence, and Organizational Resilience
items.abstract: Healthcare management is undergoing a profound transformation driven by artificial intelligence, digital technologies, evidence-based management, and increasing expectations for quality, patient safety, operational efficiency, and organizational sustainability. This conceptual article introduces the Selwan Integrated Healthcare Management Framework (SIHMF™), an integrated management model that combines artificial intelligence, data-driven decision-making, human-centered leadership, governance, organizational resilience, workforce engagement, and patient safety into a unified strategic framework for healthcare organizations. The article discusses the transition from traditional administrative models toward predictive, evidence-based management capable of anticipating risks, supporting executive decision-making, and achieving sustainable healthcare excellence. Rather than viewing digital transformation as a technological project, the framework emphasizes leadership, governance, accountability, and measurable execution as the primary drivers of successful transformation. The proposed framework may support healthcare executives, quality leaders, policymakers, researchers, and healthcare organizations seeking to integrate digital innovation with patient-centered care, organizational resilience, and strategic performance improvement.

items.title: The History and Labor of Web Scraping
items.abstract: Abstract Both the free labor of generating data online and the importance of data work which cleans, labels, and verifies these data are required for producing artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Between these two essential moments in AI production, we identify web scraping as the intercalary process of extracting data from the internet at scale. In this chapter, we highlight the essential contributions of web scraping to the production of machine learning training datasets and show that scraping is a distinct category of software labor whose understanding is important for the political economy of AI. The chapter characterizes the labor involved in both the production of scraping software and the labor required to conduct scraping operations. We provide a critical historical assessment of scraping dating back to the 1990s, tracing the development of scraping from a technical requirement for indexing the web in early communication software, to its commercialization and contemporary use in the development and production of large language models. We further describe the conditions of the labor of scraping through the analysis of contemporary documentation: industry-specific blogs, discussion boards, market reports, and conferences. We argue that the economic utility of data is dependent on its transformation from web data into datasets, and that this transformation is achieved through the labor of scraping. We suggest that the increased legal and technical barriers to the practice frame the current web scraping labor ecosystem, continuously demanding new kinds of human expertise.

items.title: The Impact of AI on Game Development: A Scoping Review of Transformations, Career Implications, and Emerging Challenges
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming the game industry by reshaping development processes, production workflows, and career structures. In this study, we present a scoping literature review examining the impact of AI on game development and employment within the industry, with particular attention to the perspectives of displacement, task transformation, and productivity effects. Drawing on academic research and industry reports published between 2020 and 2026, while retaining earlier foundational literature where relevant, this study analyzes how AI technologies such as generative AI, machine learning, procedural content generation, and large language models are integrated across major stages of game production, including game art, production management, programming, and live operations. Our findings indicate that AI can support efficiency, accelerate development cycles, and enable new forms of personalization and creative experimentation. At the same time, AI adoption may alter workforce dynamics by increasing the automation potential of routine and entry-level tasks, especially in areas such as asset creation and quality assurance. Rather than fully replacing workers, however, AI more commonly reconfigures job roles and increases demand for hybrid skill sets that combine technical knowledge, creativity, and AI literacy. Our study also identifies emerging opportunities in AI-assisted design, data analytics, and machine learning integration. Despite these benefits, AI adoption introduces important challenges related to employment polarization, intellectual property, workforce adaptation, ethical governance, and market concentration. We conclude that AI is fundamentally reshaping the game industry and highlight the need for balanced strategies that support innovation while preserving creative diversity, sustainable career pathways, and equitable access to technological opportunities. Overall, the strongest evidence concerns AI capabilities, workflow changes, and task-level transformation, whereas direct evidence of actual employment outcomes and long-term occupational change remains limited and uneven.

items.title: The impact of human-AI co-creation on perceived creativity in generative AI art: a serial mediation mechanism of psychological ownership, perceived agency, and creative flow
items.abstract: Introduction Generative AI is shifting digital art from one-step generation toward interactive human-AI co-creation. Across two between-subject experiments ( N = 600), we examined how creation mode and prespecified AI-involvement workflows related to perceived creativity. Methods In Study 1, participants completed digital art tasks under human-only creation, AI-only generation, or human-AI co-creation conditions. In Study 2, three workflows differing in AI involvement (low, moderate, high) were evaluated. Psychological ownership, perceived agency, creative flow, and perceived creativity were measured. Results In Study 1, human-AI co-creation produced higher perceived-creativity ratings than AI-only generation, with indirect effects consistent with a serial pathway through psychological ownership, perceived agency, and creative flow. In Study 2, the moderate-involvement workflow yielded higher perceived-creativity ratings and psychological states than the low- and high-involvement workflows. Discussion Perceived creativity in generative-AI art depends on how users experience contribution, control, and engagement during creation. Within the workflows tested, balancing generative assistance with consequential user choice fosters the most favorable subjective creativity evaluations.

items.title: THE LITERARY REPRESENTATION OF HUMANITY’S DECLINING SIGNIFICANCE IN CLIFFORD D. SIMAK’S NOVEL CITY
items.abstract: The article examines the representation of humanity’s declining relevance in Clifford D. Simak’s science fiction novel City, focusing on the philosophical implications of the gradual disappearance of humankind from the central position in Earth’s evolutionary and cultural development. Drawing upon posthumanist theory, ecocriticism, and literary analysis, the study explores the symbolic transformation of humans from dominant agents of civilization into mythical figures whose legacy is preserved and reinterpreted by intelligent dogs and robots. Special attention is paid to the narrative structure of the novel, in which the framing legends and episodic stories gradually undermine the reliability of human-centered historical narratives. Simak depicts technological progress not as the culmination of human achievement but as a process that ultimately renders humanity unnecessary within its own evolutionary trajectory. The emergence of autonomous robots, genetically enhanced animals, and alternative forms of intelligence illustrates the decentralization of the human subject and challenges traditional definitions of civilization, intelligence, and social organization. The article argues that City anticipates many key ideas of contemporary posthumanist thought by presenting humanity as only one temporary stage in the broader continuum of life rather than the ultimate goal of evolution. Furthermore, the novel’s ecological perspective emphasizes cooperation instead of domination, suggesting that sustainable existence depends upon mutual adaptation rather than human control over nature. Simak’s vision remains particularly relevant in the context of current discussions concerning artificial intelligence, environmental crises, and the ethical implications of technological development. The study concludes that City represents not simply the decline of humanity but the emergence of a more inclusive understanding of life, intelligence, and civilization that transcends anthropocentric limitations.

items.title: The Managerial Blind Spot Effect Explainable Machine Learning for Strategic Decision-Making
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is used in strategic decision-making; however, it is not clear whether the use of explainable machine learning leads to more managerial judgment when prediction accuracy is high. This study analyzes the proposed ‘Managerial Blind Spot Effect’ by combining predictive modelling with behavioural analysis applied to the IBM Telco Customer Churn dataset and the AI Decision Dependence and Cognitive Caution dataset. Several models, including Explanatory Boosting Machine (EBM), XGBoost, Random Forest and Neural Network, were tested, and the explanation produced by the native model EBM was enhanced by SHAP-based explanation. The behavioural results revealed that both Trust in AI and Cognitive Caution significantly contributed to an increase in AI Dependence. EBM delivered the best predictive performance with intrinsic transparency. The results highlight the importance of using explainable AI prediction models in conjunction with managerial judgment in dashboards.

items.title: The Mathematics of Deception: A Unified Framework for AI-Driven Honeypot Systems
items.abstract: Honeypots occupy a peculiar place in the security landscape: they are among the few mechanisms whose value is defined by their failure. A firewall that is never tested, an intrusion detection system that never alarms—these are successes. A honeypot that is never attacked is useless. This inversion of the usual security logic gives honeypots an unusually clean signal, but it has also kept their theoretical foundations fragmented. Game theorists model deception in isolation; information theorists treat intrusion detection generically; queuing theorists model traffic separately; and the recent wave of AI-driven honeypots—powered by Large Language Models and Reinforcement Learning—has proceeded largely without formal mathematical treatment.This paper attempts a synthesis. We develop a unified mathematical framework for AI-driven honeypot systems, building on six pillars: stochastic processes (the honeypot as a continuous time Markov chain), game theory (the honeypot as a Bayesian signaling device), detection theory (the honeypot as a near-ideal hypothesis test), information theory (the honeypot as a channel for intelligence), optimization (the honeypot as a constrained POMDP), and AI integration (LLM as observation kernel, RL as policy optimization).Along the way, we derive equilibrium conditions, detection thresholds, optimal deployment fractions, information-theoretic bounds, and LLM deception limits. We prove that the mixed strategy equilibrium is unique and Lyapunov stable, solve the POMDP for a reduced state space to obtain a threshold policy, and show that in the myopic case this threshold coincides exactly with the game-theoretic equilibrium under consistent payoff specifications. We generalize the Poisson detection assumption to a Weibull hazard model and derive a bound on the mutual information achievable under LLM-generated observations via the data processing inequality.We accompany the analytical development with numerical Monte Carlo experiments based on exact Gillespie simulation of the CTMC, replicator dynamics for the game-theoretic component, and parametric sampling for the detection and information-theoretic components. These experiments validate the closed-form predictions and expose the qualitative behavior of the system in transient and steady state. All quantitative claims are analytical; the simulations serve as numerical illustrations, not as empirical validation of real-world deployments.

items.title: The Mediating role of attitudes towards artificial intelligence in the effect of healthcare workers’ levels of cognitive flexibility on innovative work behaviour
items.abstract: BackgroundDigital transformation in healthcare requires healthcare professionals to adapt to emerging technologies and exhibit innovative work behaviors. Cognitive flexibility is an important individual characteristic that facilitates adaptation to change and innovation. However, the role of attitudes toward artificial intelligence in this relationship remains unclear.ObjectiveThis study aimed to examine the effect of healthcare professionals' cognitive flexibility on innovative work behavior and to determine the mediating role of attitudes toward artificial intelligence in this relationship.MethodsThe study employed a quantitative, cross-sectional, and correlational design. Data were collected from 532 healthcare professionals working in Konya, Türkiye, using convenience sampling. The Cognitive Flexibility Scale, Innovative Work Behavior Scale, and Artificial Intelligence Attitude Scale were used. Descriptive statistics, reliability analyses, Pearson correlation analysis, and bootstrap-based mediation analysis were conducted.ResultsCorrelation analyses revealed significant positive relationships among cognitive flexibility, attitudes toward artificial intelligence, and innovative work behavior (p < 0.001). Regression analyses demonstrated that cognitive flexibility significantly predicted both attitudes toward artificial intelligence (β=0.436, p < 0.001) and innovative work behavior (β=0.472, p < 0.001). Furthermore, bootstrap mediation analysis confirmed a statistically significant indirect effect of cognitive flexibility on innovative work behavior through attitudes toward artificial intelligence (β=0.097, 95% CI [0.075, 0.168], p < 0.001), indicating partial mediation.ConclusionsAttitudes towards artificial intelligence partially mediate the relationship between cognitive flexibility and innovative work behavior among healthcare professionals. Enhancing cognitive flexibility and fostering positive AI attitudes may contribute to supporting innovative practices and facilitating digital transformation in healthcare organizations.

items.title: The Moderating Effect of Gender on the Relationship Between Artificial Intelligence Usage, Behavioral Intentions, and Academic Engagement in Mathematics Education
items.abstract: In the age of technology, where the educational sphere and strategic advancements drive development, it is essential to understand the complex nature of gender and implement innovative tools to foster an inclusive learning environment and empower every learner. This study examines the moderating effect of gender on the relationships among Artificial Intelligence (AI) use, behavioral intentions, and academic engagement in mathematics education. Using a cross-sectional design, the study sampled 328 mathematics undergraduates from public universities in southwestern Nigeria. A structured online questionnaire hosted on Google Forms was used to collect data. The data collected were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicated that AI actual usage has a significant positive impact on behavioral academic engagement (BAE), and AI behavioral intention positively influences AI actual usage. Additionally, AI behavioral intention does not significantly influence BAE. Furthermore, AI social norms exerted large positive effects on actual AI use and behavioral intentions. In addition, gender moderates the relationship between AI behavioral intention and BAE, AI behavioral intention and AI actual usage, and AI actual usage and BAE. Therefore, educators should create specialized interventions that are responsive to the motivational and demotivational factors affecting both male and female students.

items.title: The next frontier in healthcare simulation is human-AI teaming
items.abstract: Abstract Background Across health professions, AI agents are moving out of the background and into clinical teams as collaborative entities. Yet healthcare simulation continues to conceptualise AI as a tool that serves the scenario rather than one that inhabits it. This framing is no longer adequate. The clinical environments we are preparing practitioners for demand that professionals learn to team with AI and not merely use it. Main body We contend that human-AI teaming (HAIT) is the next frontier for healthcare simulation education and research. The addition of AI agents to human teams fundamentally alters how teams communicate, work together, and accomplish goals and therefore, by extension, how we must design simulation systems for education and research. We identify five dimensions of teamwork that AI is reshaping and discuss what each means for simulation practice: communication and information exchange, shared mental models, trust calibration, team reflexivity, and team performance. We then present five imperatives that healthcare simulation must address to meet the challenges and opportunities HAIT introduces: fidelity, assessment, ethics, governance, and medico-legal framing, curriculum and faculty development, and transfer of learning. Together, these ten domains constitute a research and education agenda for a field built on the science and art of preparation. Conclusion HAIT is an emerging clinical reality and the next frontier for healthcare simulation. We call on the simulation community to treat it as a first-order priority and to focus on developing fidelity standards for AI agents in simulation, validating human-AI teaming assessment tools, establishing ethical frameworks for AI-inclusive scenario design, investing in curriculum and faculty development, and committing to the research needed to establish whether HAIT-based simulation training translates into improved performance in AI-augmented clinical practice.

items.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DEVELOPING PROFESSIONAL COMMUNICATION COMPETENCE IN ESP
items.abstract: This thesis examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in developing professional communication competence among students studying English for Specific Purposes (ESP). It explores how AI-powered tools can support the development of speaking, writing, vocabulary, and interactional skills required in professional environments. Particular attention is paid to personalized learning, simulated professional communication, and immediate feedback. The thesis also considers the challenges associated with AI integration, including the reliability of generated information, overdependence on technology, and academic integrity. It argues that the effective use of AI, combined with teacher guidance and learner autonomy, can contribute to preparing students for professional communication in English.

items.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DOCUMENTING RELIGIOUS CULTURAL HERITAGE: A STUDY OF ITS POTENTIALS AND CHALLENGES
items.abstract: This study explores how artificial intelligence (AI) technologies can be employed to effectively enhance and document religious beliefs and practices. AI has the capability to process vast amounts of religious texts and sources, enabling the efficient extraction of significant information and patterns. Additionally, it facilitates the digitalization of religious heritage, ensuring its preservation for future generations. Smart applications also contribute to improving access to religious knowledge and fostering understanding between different cultures and religions. The use of AI in this field faces several challenges, including the need to consider the sensitivity of religious beliefs and rituals to avoid any negative reactions. Moreover, reliance on automated analysis may lead to the loss of cultural and spiritual context in traditional practices. Ensuring accuracy and avoiding bias is essential to preserving authentic values. Despite these challenges, AI offers promising opportunities for documenting religious heritage, provided that a balanced approach is adopted—one that acknowledges potential risks and respects the privacy and sanctity of religious beliefs.

items.title: The role of artificial intelligence in the modern Russian economy innovative development
items.abstract: Innovation is now not just one of the possible paths of development, but the main condition for the survival of any enterprise. The key factor that changes the paradigm of the innovation process is the ability to delegate routine operations. Previously, a significant portion of highly qualified employees’ time was spent on data collection and preliminary information processing, which considerably slowed down the research and development cycle. Modern technologies make it possible to completely delegate trivial tasks to intelligent systems, which are capable of processing such information much faster than a human. In today’s environment, the integration of autonomous intelligent systems is crucial for reducing operational costs. In 2026, artificial intelligence has transformed from an auxiliary technology into an indispensable tool for ensuring the competitiveness of knowledge intensive enterprises. The main areas of application of artificial intelligence have been analyzed, including the automation of business processes, generative design, and predictive analytics of production equipment. The main barriers that limit the implementation of automation systems based on artificial intelligence have been systematized and identified. It has been established that artificial intelligence has changed the methodology of research and development work, reducing the product development cycle from several months to several weeks. The conclusion is formulated that the integration of artificial intelligence tools into production processes reduces costs, the percentage of defective products, and requires staff to develop creative and strategic competencies. The role of artificial intelligence is defined not merely as an automation tool, but as an active participant in the innovation process, capable of creating innovative solutions. An author’s classification of barriers to the implementation of artificial intelligence in knowledge intensive industries has been developed.

items.title: The role of augmented reality in smart warehousing and supply chain optimisation
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of global supply chains (SC) under the Industry 4.0 (I4.0) paradigm has intensified the demand for efficiency, accuracy, and resilience in warehousing operations. Smart warehousing has emerged as a key driver of supply chain optimisation (SCO), integrating advanced digital tools to streamline inventory management, order fulfilment, and logistics coordination. Among these technologies, augmented reality (AR) has gained prominence due to its unique capability to enhance human performance by overlaying digital information onto the physical environment. Despite an increasing interest in related areas, there remains a lack of comprehensive understanding of how AR technologies are being integrated into SC initiatives under the I4.0 umbrella. To address this, the present study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of literature published between 2015 and 2025, using the “Web of Science” and “Scopus” databases as the primary sources. A total of 51 peer-reviewed articles were identified using a structured search query combining terms related to AR, I4.0, and SC optimisation. This work contributes by offering a comprehensive synthesis of the opportunities, challenges, and future directions of AR in smart warehousing. It provides actionable insights for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers seeking to leverage AR as a strategic tool for SC optimisation in the era of I4.0.

items.title: The Role of Digital Capabilities and Human Factors in Enhancing Port Service Performance: A Mediated Model for Eastern Indonesia
items.abstract: This research was conducted in response to the increasingly urgent need for digital transformation in port services in Eastern Indonesia to improve efficiency, transparency, and service quality amid the development of information technology. The research addresses a significant gap by integrating digital capabilities and human factors within the context of port digital transformation in Eastern Indonesia, an underexplored area in the existing literature. The research objective was to examine the influence of digital capabilities, human factors, and information system success on improvements in port service performance. The research method used a quantitative approach, with surveys of service users and system managers to measure technology acceptance and information system success. The number of respondents was 189. The use of a quantitative approach, including surveys and SEM-PLS analysis, is appropriate for testing complex relationships among variables. Based on the measurements, service performance (SP) obtained the highest score (R² = 0.732), supported by the organization's strong digital capabilities, effective human resources, and successful implementation of information systems. The anticipated outcomes include identifying critical factors that determine the success of digital transformation and developing an integrative model to guide the effective implementation of port services. The model linking digital capabilities, human factors, information system success, and port service performance provides a valuable framework for future empirical research.
